lesson_title: Family Trees, Venn Circles and the Box: Geometry and Probability Essentials
hook_text: 25 take Maths. 18 take Science. That's 43 learners... in a class of 40?!
clip_script: In a class of forty, twenty-five take mathematics, eighteen take science, ten take both. How many take mathematics or science? Not twenty-five plus eighteen — that counts the ten overlap learners twice. Correct count: twenty-five plus eighteen minus ten — thirty-three. And so seven take neither. The Venn diagram shows it instantly: fill the overlap FIRST with ten, then mathematics-only is fifteen, science-only is eight, and the outside region holds whoever is left.
visual_style: A classroom of forty dots; two translucent circles sweep over them and ten dots caught in the overlap glow double-bright, flashing an alarm as the count hits forty-three; a single subtraction dims them back to counted-once and the total clicks to thirty-three with seven dots left outside.
mood: Puzzle energy — an impossible headcount resolved by one subtraction.
pacing: Fast setup of the impossible forty-three, freeze on the double-glowing overlap, calm satisfying fix.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson and never double-count an overlap again.
